is that how you treat me? phrase

also so that’s how it is?, is this how …?, so this is the way …, is that the way to behave?, so that’s your game?

classical

Ter. Ad. 128: Sīcine agis?
Ter. Eun. 1.2.19 (Lewis & Short)

1Sīcine: short final e (Lewis & Short sīcĭnē). The last syllable is the question particle -ne, which is short (Lewis & Short -nĕ). Catull. 64.132, sīcine mē patriīs āvectam, perfide, ab ārīs: the word opens the hexameter as a dactyl. So too 64.134 and 77.3, which Lewis & Short cites.

Sīcine agis?1

is that how you behave? so that’s your game?

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Other words

  • Sīcine …?1 — is this how …? so this is the way …? (opening a reproach)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 158: Sīcine mī obsequēns es?; Plaut. Asin. 127: Sīcine hoc fit?

    (vōx plērumque cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; semel Cic.)

    Sīc with the question particle -ne. It always opens the sentence and almost always implies a reproach; frequent in the comic writers, once in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Sīcine mī obsequēns es? — Quid vīs faciam?

    Is this how you oblige me? — What do you want me to do?Plaut. Merc. 158–158b

  • Sīcine hoc fit? forās aedibus mē ējicī?

    Is this how it goes? Me, thrown out of the house?Plaut. Asin. 127

See also what a shame!, what?!.

SourcesLewis & Short: sicine

Plautus, Asinaria 127; Mercator 158–158b. Terence, Adelphoe 128.
